what: A 16:9 video panel (32×18-cell WebGL plane) takes scroll speed (px/ms ÷ 3, max 1 — following 10% per frame) at 8% per frame and ripples from the edges by that share × .06, with hover it adds .02 at 5% per frame. The area within 15% of the diagonal from the center stays still and it gets stronger toward the outside, with x a sine of vertical position 3.2π (.6 per second) and y a sine of horizontal position (.78 per second, phase 1.7). The panel grows up to 2.5% with scroll speed. The panel is drawn in a canvas 10% wider on each side than its box so the ripples aren’t clipped

options.amp · hover: Scroll and interaction ripple strength (share of plate height), default .06 · .02
options.grow: Portion that grows with scroll, default .025
options.[data-fx-part=media]: video, img or canvas (pick one) to put on the panel — if none, a placeholder video plays with three lights drifting over a skin-colored panel (text from the element’s data-label)
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Slot for the canvas (selector) — created if none

note: Start WebGL when near the screen (50% above and below) and stop drawing when offscreen (video pauses too). Video is cropped to cover the panel. The shadow on the hand and the glow behind are done with CSS on the consuming side.

from.where: index.html .id-tile__media (original playground tile — work video panel)
